reviewer_added_requests.discovery_reason: The target reviews placement, ownership, dependency, failure, and rollback decisions in pre-implementation artifacts, while the candidate owns placement and structural-risk verdicts for module-boundary or dependency-direction changes. Its lightweight boundary does not show whether artifact review must defer, compose with, or exclude architecture review, so complete candidate material is needed.

The target explicitly reviews release artifacts, including ordering, exposure, stop authority, rollback, and forward recovery, while the candidate produces release plans, release artifacts, and go/no-go verdicts for production or irreversible deployment. Complete candidate material is needed to compare review authority, release-decision ownership, and the handoff boundary without inferring from the lightweight summary.

The target independently reviews engineering artifacts and downstream decisions, while the candidate independently reviews ChangeForge routing registries, router changes, fixture ownership, and coverage gaps. Because a routing registry or fixture is itself an engineering artifact in this repository, complete candidate material is needed to determine specialization, precedence, and any overlapping finding authority.

Implementation-preparation under the target must prove placement, reuse, dependency impact, rejected locations, and structural risk, while the candidate owns placement and architecture verdicts for module-boundary or dependency-direction changes. Complete candidate material is needed to distinguish general Brief preparation from authoritative architecture analysis and to verify the required handoff.

The target's implementation-preparation mode covers data, migration, consistency, stateful side effects, recovery, and rollback impact, while the candidate supports analysis and implementation for database, cache, queue, or search changes and returns state-ownership decisions. Complete candidate material is needed to compare analysis ownership and establish when middleware work leaves the general change-analysis boundary.

Complete candidate material is needed to separate preparatory impact analysis from formal release authority and identify the exact escalation boundary.

Complete candidate material is needed to resolve their analysis-mode overlap and the boundary between a general Engineering Brief and integration design.
